title: ceil(x, options) gives wrong results unless options are sorted
body:
`ceil` in `boltons/mathutils.py` accepts any iterable of options, but
it only works when they are already sorted ascending:

```python
>>> ceil(3, options=[10, 4, 6])
10    # expected 4
>>> ceil(3, options=iter([6, 4]))
TypeError   # expected 4
```

Expected: the smallest option greater than or equal to x, whatever
the order or type of the iterable (list, tuple, set, generator), as
`floor` already does.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: ceil() no longer sorts its options before bisecting.
